notes: The supplied it of frame to pronounce it right answers to no object morpheme and is correctly added under rule 44.

The ASV writes the negation and the modal as two separate words, so rule 35 splits them: לֹא takes only not, and he could frame belongs to כּוּן, discontinuous around the negative (rules 17, 25). No יָכֹל stands in the clause to claim the modal.
אוֹתוֹ takes the on through which laid hold reaches its object, which is one of rule 16's four families; the verb heads on the complement hold (rule 44).

In בָּעֵת הַהִיא the single written determiner that goes to הִיא and both articles are unrepresented (rules 12, 41, 47); the waw of אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁנַיִם stands between the same two numerals the English and joins (rule 42).
